newsitem.title: LEBANON: Turnover sharply up on the week in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Turnover sharply up on the week in Beirut.

text.p: Two out of three bank shares continued rising on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Thursday and dealers said sharply increased turnover reflected growing awareness of an active Beirut equities market.

Total turnover for the week, shortened to four days by the Good Friday holiday, rose sharply to 2,444,164 shares for a value of $14,490,999 against 1,077,155 shares for value of $8,708,543 during three working days last week.
"The week has been a big week for Lebanon's equity markets. We have seen substantial pickup of trading volumes," Deputy Manager Alain Balian of Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said.
BOB, which fell 3.45 percent in the last two days of the week, closed at $3.5, well above last week's closing of $3.375.
"It is a temporary phase. Some investors, seeking to realise profit are selling. Strong demand on the share will sustain BOB's rise," Balian said.
BOB, which made its debut on April 11, jumped a 61.29 percent on its issue price.
Of the two other bank shares, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose 4.1 percent to $15.75 from $15.125 while Banque Audi held steady at $20.
BLC and Audi have risen 40 percent and 34 percent respectively since their debuts nearly four months ago.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.59 percent to 134.5. The general BLOM stock index rose 0.07 percent to 914.22 and the LISPI moved up by 0.70 percent to 87.18.
"The increase in turnover has raised awareness among people in general that there is an active market in Beirut and that things are starting to happen," Balian said.
Demand for BOB in the week ranged from 3,399,390 shares to 1.2 million against supply of up to 629,606.
Turnover in Audi shares rose to 947,449 from 135,124 in the three trading days last week. This included an 850,000 block of shares traded at $20 on the BSE.
Some 262,404 BLC shares were traded against last week's 35,908. These included 208,893 shares traded in blocks on the bourse.
Solidere A and B were unchanged at $10.25 and $10.75.
Of the four industrial shares, Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125, pipemaker Eternit was unchanged at $2.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic and Ciments Blancs.
